doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07

title: Billie's first records
summary: Billie recalls the first record session upstairs, with Albert Jiles, Mealy and others, for Alden and David's label.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Say, Billy, when was the first time you ever made any records?
The first time I made records? Let me see, who was that first time I made a record?
Were you there somewhere on Barone Street somewhere? Were you there somewhere somewhere on Barone Street?
Were you there somewhere on Barone Street? He didn't carry that kind of way.
Was I there?
Yeah, wasn't he there? I imagine so.
I don't know. Kalinsky, was that the man?
The violin teacher, Barone Street?
Yeah, I remember Barone Street. What year was it, do you remember? Just about.
I'm making a thing, we started playing some mocha, we went upstairs, if I'm not mistaken.
We went upstairs somewhere, old band, old band, old band, I'm trying to think, me, old band, Albert Glennon, George Henderson.
It was George?
No, George, it was Albert Jive, Albert Jive cut it with us, George couldn't make it, Albert Jive, Albert made it with us.
Albert Jive for two years.

But anyhow, it was Albert Glennon and the drummer, it was Albert Jive, he had that thing. Clarinet? Mealy's old clarinet, yeah. Trombone? Harrison Brazler. How many trumpets? Dee and, uh, and, uh, Lawrence, Lawrence and Diddy.
Well that was for those two kids, uh, young boys, Alden and David, uh.
Yeah, I believe that who that was. All of us, David.
Lawrence played some and I played some, that's the way it works. Yeah.
And that's a record you got over there with Ernest's name on it, huh? Ernest. Yeah, it's got Ernest's address written on it. Oh, no, that's just, that's, yeah, yeah, yeah.
That's the same record, huh? Right over there. Take that record then.
It's got All of Me and.
Yeah, All of Me and, uh, Hell of Bob.
Callous Love, Hell of Bob. Billy Diddy's Blues.
And there was some more, my name is Rick. I believe Heikon had them records. I got some more records. The first records I got. Bill, Bill had them.
Oh, they got my, I got my picture on, on the envelope. That's right.
Well that's the ones that came out on Bill's label, but Alden and David. Yeah. Yeah. The two young kids put up the money. I was there, huh?
Yeah, well I just remember when I've been along, yeah, well you know many times.
